= Paragraph metadata

See <<normal-right>>, <<normal-center>>, <<normal-justify>>, <<normal-left>>, <<quote>>, <<verse>>, <<literal>>, <<listing>>, <<source>>, <<example>>, and <<abstract>>.

[#normal-right.text-left.text-right]
.Normal *right* title
The last applicable role aligns this paragraph to the right.

[#normal-center.text-center]
.Normal *center* title
This paragraph is centred.

[#normal-justify.text-justify]
.Normal *justified* title
This is a long paragraph with enough words to wrap onto more than one line so the explicit justify role has a visible effect in the generated PDF output.

[#normal-left.text-left]
.Normal *left* title
This paragraph is explicitly aligned to the left.

[quote#quote.text-right, Ada Lovelace, Notes]
.Quote *title*
The quote body is aligned to the right while its attribution keeps the default alignment.

[verse#verse.text-right, Emily Dickinson, Poem 1]
.Verse *title*
The verse body is aligned to the right
across both of its lines.

[literal#literal.text-right]
.Literal *title*
literal paragraph ignores alignment roles

[listing#listing.text-right]
.Listing *title*
listing paragraph ignores alignment roles

[source#source.text-right,rust]
.Source *title*
let alignment = "ignored";

[example#example.text-right]
.Example *title*
The example body is aligned to the right.

[abstract#abstract.text-right]
.Abstract *title*
The abstract body is aligned to the right.
